messages.subject: question on annotate function
parts:
Hi,

I have a simple question -- how do I justify text with the annotate
function? Annotate seems to center text at the x and y point. What if
I want to left justify at that point?

Thanks,

Walt

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: question on annotate function
parts:
Hi:

Add the argument hjust = 0 in the annotate() call. Here's an example
modified from its help page:

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
p + annotate("text", x = 4, y = 25, label = "Some text") # center justified
last_plot() + annotate('text', x = 4, y = 23, label = 'More text',
hjust = 0) # left justified

Dennis

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: question on annotate function
parts:
Same trick, but you have to use the theming system. Toy example:

DF <- data.frame(x = seq(10), y = rnorm(10))
ggplot(DF, aes(x = x, y = y)) + geom_point() + ggtitle("A title") +
theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0))

Is that what you had in mind?

Dennis
